tools.name: frame
tools.description:
Get the frame at a timestamp — Return the picture at a video time, base64'd inside the envelope, or as
raw image/jpeg with `?format=jpeg` / `Accept: image/jpeg` (the envelope's
fields then ride X-Frame-* headers). The picture is the stored keyframe
NEAREST the time (Arrow keeps one per second), not the covering scene's.

This is the Glance grain: the nearest stored keyframe, 480 px wide. Good for
orientation and for checking whether a caption is describing this picture at
all. Not good for reading small on-screen text — that wants a
native-resolution burst, and even then only when the text is missed for a
temporal reason.

Two fields exist to stop the caller over-claiming, and both must be read:
`approx_within_s` is how far this picture is from the time you asked for
(null = unknown, treat as large), and `fallback=true` means your moment had
no frame and a different one was substituted — do not cite it as the
requested timestamp.

tools.name: get_index_options
tools.description:
Indexing options: stages, values, defaults and this workspace's settings — What an arrow index run can do and will do here: `stages` (id, description,
default, available + reason, the values each takes), `defaults` (the
deployment's), `workspace` (this workspace's overrides, PUT below), `effective`
(what an upload with no `options` runs) and the JSON `schema` of an options object.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description:
Get one page of a document — A document's page `page` (1-based; page n is frame n-1, so frame_url
serves its render): its text, its reading-order passages with their boxes
and every region on it (objects, faces, text spans), all normalized with a
TOP-LEFT origin. 404 for a video / image or a page out of range.

tools.name: get_person
tools.description: A person: faces and where they appear

tools.name: get_regions
tools.description:
Get the regions of an asset (objects, faces, text) — Every box the index holds for an image, a document or a video frame:
`objects` (detected regions), `faces` (each with `cluster_id`, its face
cluster in this asset, and `person_id`, its workspace person; either is null
while there is none) and `text` (OCR spans). Boxes are {x, y, w, h},
normalized, TOP-LEFT origin.

timestamp.description: Only the frame at this time

tools.name: get_video
tools.description: Get video detail

full.description: Return the whole detail (every scene, transcript segment and description). Default false: the video's summary plus counts; use the scenes / transcript / shots tools for the lists.

tools.name: health

tools.name: list_engines
tools.description:
List search engines — The dense engines `engine` accepts on /search: [{id, recipe, status,
default, workspace_default, deployment_default, available}], for the
CALLER's workspace. `status`: "current" (arrow: every upload is indexed by
it) or "deprecated" (classic: answers only for older libraries); `default` = what this workspace's /search with no
`engine` runs (its setting, else the deployment's); `workspace_default` =
this workspace is set to it; `deployment_default` = what a workspace with no
setting gets; `available` = this API has that engine configured.

tools.name: list_people
tools.description:
List the workspace's people — The workspace's People: one id per person across its videos, images and
documents. They form on their own: after each ingest the asset's faces join the
people they match, then the workspace's faces are re-clustered: the ones no one
took form new People (3 or more alike make one) and unnamed People may be
regrouped (named ones only gain faces), so no POST /people/recluster is needed (a library
past 20,000 usable faces leaves that step to it). `people`: [{person_id, name,
status, face_count, cover_face_id, cover_url}], named first, then by face
count; status is "unverified" (formed automatically, not named yet), "named",
or "hidden" (listed only with include_hidden=true).

include_hidden.description: Also list the people you hid

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: List videos (paginated)

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description:
List workspaces this key can access — The workspaces this key may operate on: its access list (its home, plus the
read-only demo libraries and the owner's workspaces it was granted in the
dashboard, Settings > API access). Target one per request by sending
`X-Workspace-Id: <workspace_id>`. A dashboard sign-in instead of a key lists the
user's workspaces and the demos, i.e. what a key can be granted.

tools.name: magic_search
tools.description:
Magic search (character, location, music, emotion) — Magic search by type: character, location, music, or emotion.

Accepts JSON body with keys: query, video_id, cluster_id, source_video_id, limit.
Search by an uploaded face image or audio clip is not part of the public API.

On Arrow-indexed workspaces: location = captions + shot labels; emotion =
captions + emotion-linked sounds and mood music (facial expression is not
indexed); music = genre / instrument sound events + music segments (song
title / artist identification is not available); character = People by
name or person id, or a face cluster by cluster_id + source_video_id
(neither a query nor a cluster_id: 400 validation_error). `meta.search`
names the legs that served and, under `unavailable`, what the type could
not use.

search_type.description: What to search by: character (a person or face), location (a place), music (on Arrow: genres, instruments and music segments, no song identification), emotion (on Arrow: a mood in the captions, sounds and music; facial expression is not indexed).

query.description: What to find (a name, place, mood, or track)

cluster_id.description: Face/voice cluster id, when refining by example

tools.name: music_tracks

Get identified music tracks — Songs identified in the asset (title, artist). Song identification needs a
licensed fingerprint provider; Arrow has none, so this is empty for Arrow
assets. For music on the timeline use audio-segments (`audio_type` music) and
sound-events (genres, instruments).

tools.name: recall_ask

Ask a question about one video — Ask a question about ONE video: video-scoped agent chat over its indexed
data (the workspace's search engine, transcript, scenes, document pages),
answered with time-coded citations. 404 when the video is not visible to
this workspace; 502 chat_unavailable when the answer model fails.

Accepts JSON body with keys: query (str), max_tokens (int, optional).

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Semantic search across videos — Rank moments across the workspace's videos, images and documents for a
natural-language `query`. On Arrow, a whole-workspace search also reads the
transcripts: a quote of what was said (two or more words, stopwords aside:
the phrase as said, or from three words on all of them close together in
one transcript segment, three quarters of them past four) ranks the moment
it was said first, as a hit with `source` "transcript", `text` the spoken
line and `timestamp` its start. A one-word query and a within-video search
(`video_id`) rank as before.

video_id.description: Restrict search to a single video

moments_per_video.description: Up to this many moments per video (1-10), each a separate hit with its own timestamp; moments of one video closer than the moment gap are merged into one. Default 1: the single best moment per video. `limit` counts moments. Ignored with video_id (a within-video search already returns every matching moment).

search_options.description: DEPRECATED and ignored: accepted for compatibility, no option is read

rerank.description: DEPRECATED and ignored: no cross-encoder reranking runs on /api/v1/search

workspace_ids.description: Search across multiple workspaces and merge into one ranked list — each result carries its own workspace_id. Only workspaces this key can read are queried. Omit to search the single active workspace.

engine.description: Search engine: 'arrow' (current: SigLIP2 frames under F.O.C.A.L. + Gemma captions, plus a speech step on a whole-workspace search: a spoken quote ranks the moment it was said first, as a `source: "transcript"` hit; searches what Arrow indexed, including images and document pages, with page / region / passage on each hit) or 'classic' (DEPRECATED: answers only for older libraries; removal will be announced in the changelog). Omit for the workspace's default (federated: each workspace's own). GET /api/v1/engines lists them. The response's `engine` says which one answered (null when no dense engine did) and `recipe` its recipe id; if the requested engine cannot serve, classic answers where the workspace holds classic-indexed videos, else the fallback tiers do (`engine` null, `source` "rrf" or "lexical"), and `engine_fallback` carries a code: <engine>_not_configured | _breaker_open | _not_ready | _partial | _recipe_mismatch | _no_active_leg | _timeout | _unavailable.

tools.name: shots
tools.description:
Get shot metadata — One row per shot (scene). On Arrow assets (every upload now) only
`num_people` (faces stage) and `visible_text` (OCR stage) are filled:
shot_scale, camera_angle, shot_type, setting_indoor, setting_daytime, mood,
objects and actions are null or empty.
